title: bug: moe-proxy comparableProjectPath maps /mnt/<d> on the raw string, so a relative or non-normalized MOE_PROJECT_PATH is refused as "a different project"
description:
packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts comparableProjectPath runs the /mnt/<letter> regex on the raw string, so a path that has to go through path.resolve is never mapped. With cwd /mnt/d/projexts/app: '.' becomes '/mnt/d/projexts/app', '/mnt/d/projexts/app/.' becomes 'd:/projexts/app/.', and '/mnt/d/projexts/app/sub/..' becomes 'd:/projexts/app/sub/..'. All of these differ from 'd:/projexts/app', so readDaemonInfoResult answers "daemon.json belongs to a different project" and the proxy exits. Reproduced with tsx while working on task-a60a1616 QA round 1. It is non-destructive, and the launchers pass absolute paths.
Fix: resolve first, then map; on win32, posix-normalize a raw /mnt path. This mirrors the daemon fix in task-a60a1616 (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts comparableProjectPath, test rows X9/X10).
definitionOfDone: With cwd /mnt/d/x, moe-proxy comparableProjectPath gives 'd:/x' for '.', '/mnt/d/x/.', '/mnt/d/x/sub/..' and '/mnt/d//x', matching '/mnt/d/x' and 'D:\\x'.
On win32, a raw '/mnt/<d>/…' path is posix-normalized before it is mapped.
Existing moe-proxy utils tests stay green. New rows in packages/moe-proxy cover relative and non-normalized inputs and are red before the fix.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN, in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts. Port the daemon's rule (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts comparableProjectPath, landed by task-a60a1616) into comparableProjectPath. Keep its export, its signature, the proxy file's brace style and normalizeWindowsDrivePath. The order is:
1. raw = projectPath.trim(). The existing drive regex still detects a drive path on the RAW string and returns normalizeWindowsDrivePath(raw), because path.resolve would treat it as relative on Linux.
2. const isWin32 = process.platform === 'win32', read on every call (T2 flips it). const resolved = path.resolve(raw).
3. Run the existing /mnt regex on `isWin32 ? path.posix.normalize(raw) : resolved`.
   - On POSIX it maps after resolving.
   - On win32 it posix-normalizes the raw string, because path.resolve would prefix a /mnt path with the cwd drive.
   - Keep the trailing-slash strip on the captured rest (posix.normalize keeps a trailing '/') and the lowercase.
4. Everything else is unchanged. A drive-form `resolved` goes through normalizeWindowsDrivePath. Otherwise return `resolved`, lowercased only on win32.

Delete the stale 'Both special forms are detected on the RAW string' comment. Rewrite the JSDoc to state the rule:
- the drive form is detected on the raw string;
- /mnt/<d> is mapped only after normalizing, so '.', 'sub/..' and '/mnt/d/x/./' match '/mnt/d/x';
- win32 uses a posix normalize;
- the daemon's copy follows the same rule.

Change nothing else in utils.ts. isSameProjectPath, readDaemonInfoResult and its 'daemon.json belongs to a different project' text stay as they are.

Error handling: the function stays pure and synchronous, with no IO and no new throw path. readDaemonInfoResult's try/catch is untouched.

Copy utils.ts into the step-1 snapshot, cmp it, and run `npx vitest run src/utils.test.ts` there. T1, T2 and every existing readDaemonInfo/comparableProjectPath test must pass.

Out of scope, do not touch: the daemon, and scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs (an older port that keeps the raw-string rule).
implementationPlan.note: Ported daemon rule. Snapshot run: 87/87 pass, cmp clean.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review and read the two-file diff as an attacker.

1. Mutation probes. Work in a scratch copy of the gate snapshot: copy it without node_modules, then symlink node_modules back. Apply each mutant alone and run `npx vitest run src/utils.test.ts`.
   (a) HEAD's utils.ts: T1 and T2 fail.
   (b) win32 uses `resolved` instead of path.posix.normalize(raw): T2 fails, because the win32 stand-in resolves '/mnt/d/x/sub/..' to 'C:\mnt\d\x'.
   (c) path.posix.normalize(raw) on every platform, with no resolve first: T1 fails on '.' and 'sub/..'.
   (d) no trailing-slash strip: T2 fails on '/mnt/d/x/./'.
   A surviving mutant means a weak assertion. Strengthen the test, never the mutant.
2. Parity: the proxy body and packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts comparableProjectPath implement the same rule.
3. Inputs:
   - '' and whitespace still resolve to the cwd, as before.
   - '/mnt', '/mnt/' and '/mnt/dd/x' are not mapped.
   - '/mnt/D/X' is lowercased.
   - '/mnt/d/..' resolves to '/mnt', which is not mapped.
   - A drive path with '..' still takes the raw branch.
4. Test hygiene:
   - the cwd spy and the path.resolve spy are restored on every path (afterEach plus finally);
   - the platform descriptor is restored in finally;
   - no test reads or writes a real .moe directory.
5. Concurrency: the function is pure and synchronous and reads process.platform and process.cwd() per call, so concurrent proxies cannot interfere.
6. Scope: only the two files changed. There is no dist, package.json or lockfile change, and the shared dist stat is unchanged.

Record the findings and fixes in the step note.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe-proxy comparableProjectPath maps /mnt/<d> only after normalizing: on POSIX after path.resolve, on win32 after path.posix.normalize of the raw string. A relative or non-normalized MOE_PROJECT_PATH that names the same directory as daemon.json's recorded projectPath is no longer refused as 'daemon.json belongs to a different project'.
acceptanceCriteria: On POSIX with process.cwd() = '/mnt/d/x', comparableProjectPath returns 'd:/x' for '.', '/mnt/d/x/.', '/mnt/d/x/sub/..', '/mnt/d//x', 'sub/..', '/mnt/d/x/./', '/mnt/d/x' and 'D:\\x'; it returns 'd:/x/sub' for 'sub' and 'd:' for '..'.
With process.platform = 'win32' (emulated off Windows with a win32 path.resolve stand-in), '/mnt/d/x/sub/..', '/mnt/d/x/./' and '/mnt/d//x' return 'd:/x', and '/mnt/d/x/sub/../..' returns 'd:'.
Both new tests fail on HEAD's utils.ts; every pre-existing utils.test.ts test passes unchanged.
invariants: A drive-letter path is detected on the raw string and normalized with path.win32.
A path that is neither /mnt/<d> nor drive-form keeps its old result: path.resolve, lowercased only on win32.
comparableProjectPath stays pure and synchronous and reads process.platform and process.cwd() per call.
readDaemonInfoResult's results and error texts are unchanged, except that more same-project path forms now match.
compatibility: The exported signature comparableProjectPath(projectPath: string): string is unchanged.
No daemon.json shape, MCP wire or launcher change.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: port the daemon's fixed rule (task-a60a1616) in logic, so both readers of daemon.json agree. Rejected:
(1) path.posix.normalize everywhere. On POSIX a relative '.' or 'sub/..' must be resolved against the cwd before mapping.
(2) path.resolve on win32. It prefixes a /mnt path with the cwd drive, giving 'c:/mnt/d/x'.
(3) A shared helper module for daemon and proxy. There are no npm workspaces and no shared package, so it is a cross-package refactor outside this LOW bug.
(4) New rows in a new test file to dodge the contested utils.test.ts. utils.ts is contested anyway, and the rows belong beside the existing describe.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- comparableProjectPath (utils.ts ~24-44) only feeds isSameProjectPath, which feeds readDaemonInfoResult. index.ts calls that with getProjectPath() = MOE_PROJECT_PATH || process.cwd(), unresolved.
- The launchers pass absolute paths, so the bug only bites a hand-set relative or non-normalized MOE_PROJECT_PATH. It is non-destructive: the proxy exits with 'daemon.json belongs to a different project'.
- The daemon's copy (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts ~100-113) is the reference. X9/X10 in index.test.ts (~374-407) pin it.
- utils.ts default-imports path, so vi.spyOn(path, 'resolve') in the test sees its calls.
- The proxy tsconfig includes src, so tsc type-checks the tests during pretest. vitest.config.ts blanks the seat's MOE_* env.
- Reproduced at plan time against the built proxy with cwd /mnt/d/projexts/moes: '.' gave '/mnt/d/projexts/moes', '<cwd>/.' gave 'd:/projexts/moes/.', '<cwd>/sub/..' gave 'd:/projexts/moes/sub/..', and '/mnt/d//projexts/moes' gave 'd://projexts/moes'.
- A scratch port of the fixed rule produced exactly the T1/T2 values in step 1. Mutant (b) yields 'C:\mnt\d\x' under the win32 stand-in.
